title: Mischief Makers
subtitle: Grab first, ask later
summary: Mischief Makers is Treasure’s exuberant side-scrolling platform game for Nintendo 64. Marina Liteyears, a robotic maid, sets out to rescue her kidnapped creator, Professor Theo, on the planet Clancer. The adventure uses pre-rendered sprites and three-dimensional scenery, but its central idea is wonderfully physical: Marina can grab things, shake them and throw them. body: Mischief Makers is Treasure’s exuberant side-scrolling platform game for Nintendo 64. Marina Liteyears, a robotic maid, sets out to rescue her kidnapped creator, Professor Theo, on the planet Clancer. The adventure uses pre-rendered sprites and three-dimensional scenery, but its central idea is wonderfully physical: Marina can grab things, shake them and throw them. Enemies and objects become material for solving problems. Across five worlds and fifty-two stages, a small set of actions is repeatedly turned into a different kind of challenge.

Picking something up rarely settles what to do with it. Shaking can reveal an item or change how an object works; throwing can clear a threat or provide a solution elsewhere. Marina’s movement adds running, jumping and directional boosts to the same toolkit. A scene that first resembles a conventional platform obstacle can therefore become a question about handling its contents. Treasure builds variety by changing the circumstances around these actions, allowing familiar controls to support races, encounters and more playful interruptions.

Clearing a stage leaves room for a more demanding visit. Yellow gems reward additional discoveries and affect how much of the ending is shown, encouraging players to look beyond the immediate exit. The game’s character comes from this willingness to hide another use inside something already seen. Its expressive sprites and sudden changes of pace support the same idea: the world is available to be handled. Mischief Makers makes experimentation feel like part of Marina’s personality, rather than a separate layer of optional tasks.
